transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (HorizonMed VP Procurement), Ethan Cho (HorizonMed Head of Security), Priya Nair (HorizonMed Dir ML Ops), Noah Reed (HorizonMed Finance)

Auto-summary: discussed MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, dedicated capacity pricing, security artifacts and next steps to send documents and schedule pilot.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 
 this is Lena from Redwood, i have Samir here from our se team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maria Gonzalez: Hi Lena, thanks. All good. We've got a few people on our side, i'll hand off to Priya for the technical bits later.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Good afternoon all, quick agenda 
 MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs, pricing questions and then pilot/onboarding timeline. We'll try to keep this tight.
[00:25] Ethan Cho: Sounds good, security will focus on DPA and KMS details.
[00:30] Priya Nair: And i'll talk about expected workloads and what we'd want to benchmark.

[02:05] Lena Park: To start 
 Maria you sent a marked-up MSA and a DPA with a couple of edits around data retention and breach notification. We reviewed those, and we highlighted a few items where we can be flexible. Biggest asks we saw were shorter breach notification windows and additional logging/audit retention.
[02:25] Maria Gonzalez: Yes, breach notification 
 we need 24 hours and an SLA that includes forensic support for at least 30 days. Is that in scope?
[02:33] Samir Patel: We usually support 72 hours notification in our standard MSA, 24 hours is pretty tight. We can commit to 48 hours for HorizonMed and include forensic support escalation path. I will flag that for legal but want to call it out as an exception. (slight hesitation)
[02:55] Ethan Cho: 48 is reasonable, but we also need proof of traceability 
 audit logs accessible for 13 months.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Audit logs retention 
 default is 12 months, we can extend to 13 months as an addendum. We'll need to check on storage costs for extended retention.

[04:10] Priya Nair: On the DPA side, we need clarity on subprocessors, where data is stored (region) and whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[04:25] Samir Patel: Yes 
 we have Private deployment options with customer-managed KMS/HSM integration. For hosted, we offer region pinning and bring-your-own-key via partner KMS. There's some variation between Hosted and Dedicated.
[04:40] Lena Park: To clarify, the options: Hosted 
 fastest onboarding, shared infra, region pinning and BYOK but limited guarantees on isolation. Dedicated 
 reserved GPU pools, physical isolation, custom KMS and stronger SLA.

[06:05] Noah Reed: Pricing question 
 if we go Dedicated, what are our commit levels and is there a quarterly true-up?
[06:12] Lena Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity billed monthly with a minimum 12-month commit for enterprise deals. We typically do monthly usage reporting and an annual audit for commit levels; true-ups are handled quarterly.
[06:25] Noah Reed: Ok, we'll need a spreadsheet with pricing tiers, examples for projected QPS and cost per 1M tokens so procurement can model it.
[06:33] Lena Park: We will share the pricing workbook after this call 
 i'll include committed vs metered scenarios and an example with caching/batching assumptions.

[07:50] Ethan Cho: Security artifacts 
 do you have SOC 2 Type II and a recent pentest? We need the reports and any remediation timelines.
[07:58] Samir Patel: Yes we have SOC 2 Type II, and a pen test from last quarter. I'll upload those to a secure link with an NDA filter 
 should be able to send by Friday.
[08:08] Maria Gonzalez: Perfect. Also do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for our org?
[08:13] Samir Patel: Yes SSO via SAML and OIDC, role-based access control is supported in the Console with token-level audit trails.

[09:42] Priya Nair: For pilot scope 
 we're thinking 3 model endpoints, about 10k QPS peak across a week-long test, representative sample dataset of PHI-sanitized clinical notes. We want to validate latency at 99th pctl and cost per token.
[09:58] Samir Patel: 10k QPS is sizable 
 can you confirm whether that's concurrent requests or per-minute? Also, sequence lengths and typical prompt/response sizes?
[10:08] Priya Nair: It's peak concurrent requests, typical prompts avg 250 tokens, responses about 150 tokens. We want 99th pctl latency under 300ms for the critical route.
[10:22] Samir Patel: Understood. For 300ms 99th pctl at that token size, Dedicated with tuned batching and KV cache will be more reliable. On Hosted we can try but it's a best-effort. We'll include recommended quantization and batching configs in the pilot plan.

[12:15] Maria Gonzalez: About compliance 
 we have data residency constraints for EMEA patients, we might need on-prem or VPC in eu-west.
[12:24] Lena Park: We can provision Private deployments in eu-west and provide an on-prem package if required. That does increase lead time for onboarding 
 usually 6-8 weeks for on-prem vs 1-2 weeks for hosted.

[13:50] Priya Nair: Also curious about model fallbacks and graceful degradation. If a model goes OOM or overloaded, can Redwood automatically route to a cheaper or smaller variant?
[13:59] Samir Patel: Yes 
 we have smart routing and automated fallback policies. We'll show an example in the ops runbook 
 you can do canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback to a compatible variant. Sometimes transcription shows "KV cache" as "K V cash" but yes it's supported.

[15:05] Noah Reed: On billing 
 is there detailed token-level billing and cost attribution by route? We need to map costs to product teams.
[15:12] Lena Park: Yes 
 Console has token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards and nightly CSV exports for chargeback. We'll include a sample export.

[16:45] Maria Gonzalez: For legal timeline 
 if we get a vendor redline by next week, how long until we can finalize? Our procurement committee meets 2027-07-29.
[16:52] Lena Park: If we get redlines by 2027-07-27, legal can turn around in 3 business days. So that should align with your committee on 07-29.

[18:00] Priya Nair: A couple of nitty-gritty items on the DPA 
 data deletion certificates, subprocessors list and ability to restrict subprocessor locations.
[18:10] Samir Patel: We'll provide a subprocessors list and can include a clause to restrict to approved regions. Data deletion certificates are part of the offboarding API. We'll share sample certs.

[20:00] (brief side conversation)
[20:12] Maria Gonzalez: One more thing 
 are there any primary competitors you're worried we'll ask about?
[20:17] Lena Park: Customers often compare to OpenAI and Anthropic for model quality, and Google Cloud AI for infrastructure bundles. We'll provide our differentiation doc focused on production economics.

[22:30] Samir Patel: Quick demo note 
 for the pilot we'll run two scenarios: 1) hosted rapid validation using a pinned region and BYOK, and 2) dedicated cluster with reserved GPUs to hit the 300ms 99th pctl requirement. We'll run latency/throughput traces and provide token-level cost breakdowns.

[24:40] Priya Nair: Can you do deterministic reproducibility? We often need prompt reproducibility across runs for audits.
[24:47] Samir Patel: There are seeding controls and we can capture model version and prompt sets in the eval harness. We'll include eval artifacts in the pilot delivery.

[27:05] Noah Reed: On SLA numbers 
 uptime, latency SLOs and credits. What do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[27:15] Lena Park: Hosted has a 99.5% uptime SLO with standard credits for outages; Dedicated can be contracted up to 99.95% with SLA-backed credits and faster incident response. Latency SLOs can be negotiated per-route in Dedicated contracts.

[29:40] Ethan Cho: For encryption 
 both in-flight and at-rest standards? KMS integration specifics?
[29:47] Samir Patel: TLS 1.2+, per-tenant keys at rest via customer-managed KMS, HSM support for Dedicated. We'll include a technical checklist for your security team.

[32:00] Maria Gonzalez: On procurement approvals 
 we will need a statement of work and an invoice schedule. Can you provide sample SOW templates?
[32:07] Lena Park: Yes, we'll attach SOW and proposed invoice schedules (monthly or annual prepay) with the pricing workbook.

[34:20] Priya Nair: Any limits on model variant uploads? We plan to bring our own fine-tuned models.
[34:27] Samir Patel: You can bring models in Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted supports vetted model onboarding via our model catalog with a security review. We'll outline the model onboarding checklist.

[36:40] Maria Gonzalez: Ok recap then maybe run through next steps 
 Maria to review cost model with finance, Priya to send QPS and dataset details, Redwood to send redlines and security artifacts.
[36:55] Lena Park: Correct. To confirm deadlines: Redwood sends redlined MSA + DPA by 2027-07-27, SOC2 and pentest by 2027-07-22, pilot kickoff week of 2027-08-02 pending your dataset and QPS confirmation.

[38:10] (brief crosstalk)
[38:20] Noah Reed: One more finance question 
 are there any onboarding credits or trial incentives?
[38:26] Lena Park: We can offer a pilot credit to offset initial benchmarking costs 
 typical is $15k-$30k depending on pilot scope. We'll propose a credit in the pricing workbook.

[40:05] Priya Nair: Great. Also please include runbook for failover to smaller model and how we can automate rollout.
[40:12] Samir Patel: Will do, we'll include runbook and example config for smart routing and canary policies.

[42:30] Maria Gonzalez: Legal will want redlines inline, please use Track Changes or comments in the doc so it's easy for our counsel.
[42:36] Lena Park: We'll send redlines in Docx with change tracking and a PDF copy.

[44:00] Ethan Cho: For the pen test 
 any high or medium issues open currently?
[44:07] Samir Patel: No critical issues; a couple of medium findings are on a remediation timeline but not impacting data isolation. We'll include a remediation summary.

[46:00] Lena Park: Anything else before we close?
[46:05] Priya Nair: One ask 
 sample export of token-level billing to verify chargeback schema.
[46:10] Lena Park: We'll attach that.

[48:30] Maria Gonzalez: Thanks everyone 
 we'll expect the artifacts and meet the timelines.
[48:35] Lena Park: Great, thanks for your time. We'll follow up with links and calendar invite for pilot kickoff.
[48:42] (meeting ends)

Reference artifacts mentioned: redlined MSA (docx), DPA marked-up (pdf), SOC2 Type II (pdf), penetration test report (pdf), pricing workbook (xlsx), sample token-level billing export (csv), pilot SOW template (docx).

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few garbled technical terms (KV cache sometimes as "K V cash"), and occasional speaker attribution mismatch (Priya sometimes labeled Speaker 3).

End of transcript.
